text:
olivia (oncall): ap-south1 provisioning errors, multiple GPU nodes stuck in Pending. Observability shows no gpu-util metrics for that region. Noticing traffic shifted to other regions automatically. Raising incident. :warning:

sre-alerts-bot: [ALERT] kube-node-provisioner: 5 nodes failed in ap-south1 (instance quota). Link: https://internal.alerts/evt/12345

maria (eng-sre): Impact? user-facing latency or dropped requests?

olivia (oncall): We see 20% increased latency for hosted inference in AP region, 5% error spike on dedicated pools routing. No token-level failures yet but queueing increased.

sami (eng-infra): Looking at autoscaler logs. Provisioning requests rejected by cloud API due to per-project quota. Also saw repeated 502 from gpumgr-provisioner. Running `kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=region=ap-south1` now.

kevin (eng-runtime): I checked metrics pipeline — ap-south1 exporters not scraping. `kubectl logs ds/metrics-exporter -n observability` shows exporter repeatedly restarting with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` after a cert rotation.

kevin (eng-runtime): paste: ```2025-07-22T08:12:34Z metrics-exporter [WARN] failed to push metrics: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2025-07-22T08:12:36Z metrics-exporter [INFO] exiting```

nate (ml-infra): If exporters are down, autoscaler health is blind. That would explain provisioning failing (we rely on exported GPU capacity). Can we confirm telemetry egress is allowed from ap-south1 nodes?

sami (eng-infra): Running `kubectl describe netpol -n kube-system` — found a new networkpolicy applied by CNI upgrade that denies egress to 443 for `kube-system` pods. Looks like a change from the 2025-07-22 CNI roll.

olivia (oncall): That would block cert refresh to our internal CA endpoint. :grimacing:

devops-bot: Executing temporary policy patch: `kubectl patch netpol allow-e2e -n kube-system --type='json' -p='[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/egress/0"}]'` — started.

kevin (eng-runtime): Restarting metrics-exporter DaemonSet to pick up new policy.

kevin (eng-runtime): `kubectl rollout restart ds/metrics-exporter -n observability` — in progress.

sre-alerts-bot: [INFO] traffic-shift triggered to eu-west1 for latency-sensitive routes by routing-controller (policy: failover-region-available)

maria (eng-sre): Confirmed exporter pods are now stable. Metrics for ap-south1 started flowing in Grafana around +6m.

olivia (oncall): Autoscaler saw the restored metrics and retried provisioning. Cloud API accepted 3 node requests; nodes joined.

nate (ml-infra): Verified GPU pools healthy. Running a quick load test to confirm no more queueing.

sami (eng-infra): Root cause: CNI rollback/upgrade applied a stricter netpol that inadvertently blocked egress for kube-system -> internal-CA. Opened ticket INFRA-4826 to revert change and add an integration test for cert refresh flows.

maria (eng-sre): Postmortem note: observability blindspot had two compounding problems — exporter restarts (cert rotation) + netpol block. Both needed to be addressed to let autoscaler work.

olivia (oncall): Impact summary: ~12min of degraded provisioning, ~14% latency increase for AP routes during shift, no data exfiltration. Cost note: short burst of cross-region traffic to eu-west1 added ~$450 in outgoing costs. Tagging finance.

kevin (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) revert CNI netpol change (INFRA-4826) 2) add e2e for cert refresh (INFRA-4830) 3) instrument exporter health as autoscaler input (INFRA-4831)

maria (eng-sre): I'll schedule follow-up postmortem doc and include timeline + dashboard screenshots.

olivia (oncall): Thanks all. Closing incident after handover. :thumbsup:

sami (eng-infra): FYI: I've pushed a temporary rule to prevent netpol from being applied during upgrades until tests exist.

devops-bot: Incident closed by olivia (oncall). Incident ID: INC-20250722-092
